land.text: northern Gaul, where Aegidius, appointed by Majorian 'in about 457', and then his son Syagrius held Soissons

predecessors.note: The domain was nominally Roman until 476 and sits inside Cliopatria's Western Roman Empire shape to 475; Cliopatria's Soissons row begins 476. Syagrius's infobox gives 'Ruler of the Domain of Soissons 464-486'.

land.text: 'Clovis made continual war against Syagrius, and in the end took over all his territory'; the territory passed to Clovis

successors.note: Cliopatria keeps a Soissons shape to 489; the Battle of Soissons was fought in 486 (the lead of the Syagrius page: 486/487 for his death).

capitals.name: Soissons
capitals.note: Gregory of Tours: Syagrius 'had the seat of his kingdom in Soissons which his father Aegidius had somehow held'.

rulers.name: Syagrius
rulers.title: King of the Romans (Gregory of Tours); Roman patrician (Fredegar)
rulers.note: Infobox 'Ruler of the Domain of Soissons 464-486'; his father Aegidius, master of soldiers appointed by Majorian 'in about 457', died in the autumn of 464 or 465 ('In 465 Aegidius was himself murdered', Syagrius page). Only 476-486 is within this dossier.

correction.text: northern Gaul around Soissons, without the Dalmatian cells that Cliopatria joins to it; for 476-479

keyframe_review.note: 476-479 (159,048 km2): the shape joins northern Gaul (France, 524 cells, with 43 cells of Brittany) to 121 cells of Dalmatia, Croatia and Bosnia. The Dalmatian part is Julius Nepos's rump of the Western Empire ('In Dalmatia: 28 August 475 - 9 May 480', 'continued to reign as Western emperor from Dalmatia', Nepos page), not Syagrius's; it is drawn in the western-roman-empire dossier's 476 keyframe. The Gaulish part stands. The Kingdom of Soissons page gives no area and no boundary ('Not dated', 'No area is given'); the 480 shape's 125,260 km2 is the figure to use. The Armorican cells are doubtful: the Fall page has Armorica 'controlled by Bagaudae' from 400.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape unchanged for 480-486; from 487 the land is Clovis's

keyframe_review.note: 480-489 (125,260 km2): the Gaulish shape is right for its land but runs three years past the end: 'In 486, Syagrius lost the Battle of Soissons to the Frankish king Clovis I' and was executed in 486 or 487 (Soissons page); the territory passed to Clovis. Drawn for 480-486 only; 487-489 belong to the Franks.

region.text: northern Gaul with its seat at Soissons, 'the seat of his kingdom in Soissons which his father Aegidius had somehow held'

ledger.note: 476: with the last Western emperor in Italy deposed, Syagrius holds northern Gaul from Soissons. 'In 476 Odoacer dethroned Romulus Augustulus, the last sitting emperor of the Western Roman Empire, in Italy'; Gregory of Tours calls Syagrius 'King of the Romans'; the Gauls 'sent an embassy to the Eastern emperor Zeno, who chose Odoacer instead' (MacGeorge thinks Syagrius likely the sender). The page gives no founding date, calls 'Kingdom of Soissons' a modern label and treats the extent as disputed (a 'Count of Soissons' to a state controlling most of northern Gaul); the year is Cliopatria's and the date of the Western Empire's end.

region.text: the territory of Syagrius, all of which Clovis 'took over'

ledger.note: 486: Clovis defeats Syagrius at Soissons and takes his land. 'In 486, Syagrius lost the Battle of Soissons to the Frankish king Clovis I'; 'Syagrius fled to Toulouse and the protection of Alaric II' and was handed to Clovis and executed 'in 486 or 487'; 'Clovis made continual war against Syagrius, and in the end took over all his territory'. The Syagrius page: 'five years into his reign', 'in about 486'. Cliopatria's shape runs to 489.

wars.name: Battle of Soissons
wars.outcome: Clovis defeated Syagrius, who fled to Alaric II at Toulouse and was handed over and executed in 486 or 487; Clovis took over his territory.
wars.note: The Syagrius page dates the battle 'in about 486' and Clovis's attack 'five years into his reign'; the Kingdom of Soissons page counts the fifth year of Clovis as 485/486 or 486/487.

certainty.note: The pages give neither borders nor a founding date for the domain; modern historians disagree whether it was a state 'controlling most of northern Gaul' or little more than a county of Soissons. Only Soissons, Reims (Remigius), Tournai, Orleans and the Loire are named.

sources.title: Kingdom of Soissons
sources.note: Rulers (Aegidius c. 457-465, Syagrius to 486), 476 context, the Gallic embassy to Zeno, Battle of Soissons, the dispute over the nature of the state.

sources.title: Syagrius
sources.note: 'Ruler of the Domain of Soissons 464-486', the title 'King of Romans', the fall in about 486, the territory passing to Clovis.

sources.title: Julius Nepos
sources.note: Nepos in Dalmatia 475-480, for the Dalmatian cells in Cliopatria's 476-479 shape; Nepos's coinage under Syagrius in northern Gaul.

notes: Cliopatria's two shapes (476-479, 480-489) are reviewed in keyframe_review: the first joins Dalmatia to northern Gaul (it does not include Odoacer's northern Italy, as data/README.md suspected; the 121 extra cells are Croatia, Bosnia, Montenegro and Dalmatia, Nepos's rump, now in western-roman-empire_476), and both run past the page's 486. Odoacer's kingdom 476-493 is written as a new state, kingdom-of-odoacer. Start: Cliopatria's 476 is kept because the domain sits inside the Western Roman Empire shape to 475 (Nepos's coins under Syagrius in northern Gaul); the pages give the domain earlier roots (Aegidius from about 457, the infobox 464-486) that a gap-filler may prefer as the start. The infobox area is absent. The Kingdom of Soissons page has no infobox, so no area comparison was possible. Earlier wars (before 476, not listed): Aegidius 'won a battle at Orleans against the Visigoths in 463'; in about 469/470 Childeric and Count Paul fought on the Loire. Disagreements: Aegidius's death autumn 464 or 465; Syagrius's death 486 or 487; the extent (Armorica, Paris, Rouen, Angers are not named on either page). Counterpart kingdom-of-the-franks stands for Clovis's Franks (Cliopatria also has salian-franks 358-509); eu-07 should confirm. Page budget (1-2) used: two pages plus the Nepos page shared with the Western Roman Empire dossier.
